claims.text: RHEAs are candidate structural materials for high-temperature applications.
The selected RHEA should contain oxide-forming elements such as Cr, Al, or Ta.
The intervention is pre-oxidation in 1–10 mbar oxygen at 1000–1100 °C for approximately one hour.
The specified pre-oxidation treatment will form a stable, adherent oxide scale on the RHEA.
The pre-oxidation scale will be thin and dense.
The pre-oxidation scale may comprise Cr2O3, Al2O3, or mixed CrTaO4-based phases.
Al2O3 and Cr2O3 layers can provide high-temperature oxidation resistance because they are thermodynamically stable.
The preformed oxide layer acts as a slow-diffusion barrier.
The barrier limits oxygen transport into the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen transport suppresses subsequent oxidation during high-temperature air exposure.
After exposure to flowing air at 1200–1300 °C for at least 100 hours, pre-oxidized specimens will have at least 30% lower oxidation mass gain than untreated specimens.
Pre-oxidized specimens will retain better surface integrity than untreated specimens under the specified exposure.
The untreated alloy develops an irregular, less-protective oxide scale.
The untreated alloy consequently exhibits higher mass gain and an earlier onset of accelerated oxidation.
Sufficient concentrations of oxide-forming elements are required to form a stable protective scale.
Prolonged or excessively hot pre-oxidation may produce undesirable grain growth or other microstructural changes.
The magnitude of mass-gain reduction may depend on alloy composition, processing history, and control of oxygen partial pressure during pre-oxidation.
The hypothesis is falsified if pre-oxidation yields no more than a 10% mass-gain reduction or fails to produce a more coherent and continuous oxide scale.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts at least a 30% mass-gain reduction, but the mass-based falsification threshold is only 10% or less. Results between greater than 10% and less than 30% would violate the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated mass-based falsification rule.
